requirement:
A delivered read page records the dependencies retained by that page under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. Each continuation of a
node or mapped source read retains the original node identity and content
fingerprint; reading a later page does not observe a newer version. A change
to that node's fingerprint can invalidate the evidence even if it happens
between pages. Direct inspection records on return; agent tools record on
delivery. Discovery pages record no evidence inputs, just like their initial
result. Preparing an undelivered page records no read.
rationale:
I judge the reviewed tests adequate for `requirements.sdk.graph.context-tools.pages.inputs`. I did not request implementation source, because the supplied tests and their assertions settled each obligation.

Each obligation maps to tests as follows.

- **Delivered page records the dependencies that page retains.**
  - `graph_tools_record_delivered_snapshots_and_prepared_pages_do_not_record_delivery` reads an 18,000-character node and then calls `get_node_page`. It asserts exactly two observations, an edge observation and a `Dependency::Node(Node(2), …)` whose fingerprint is the full original contents.
  - It also asserts the finished record carries those same dependencies.
  - `fixed_tools_deliver_domain_contents_with_mandatory_snapshot_dependencies` covers mapped source reads. Every `get_source_page` result has `dependencies == expected`, the dependency from the initial read.
  - `source_read_pages_retain_text_and_dependencies_without_another_read` asserts each page delivers a single `Dependency::Node(Node(7), …)` carrying the original text as its fingerprint value.
- **Continuations retain the original identity and fingerprint, and a later page does not observe a newer version.**
  - `graph_read_pages_retain_the_prepared_snapshot_after_contents_change` changes the node contents between the read and the page fetch.
    - It asserts the recorded fingerprint is the original.
    - It asserts the delivered page text has no replacement text.
    - It asserts the graph was read only once.
  - The source-side tests above do the same for mapped reads. They replace the content or domain text between pages, assert the retained fingerprint and text are the originals, and count a single observation or read.
  - `direct_pages_retain_unicode_snapshots_without_rereads_or_new_dependencies` does this for direct inspection. It also checks that the dependency list stays one original-fingerprint entry across all pages and that `reads == [1]`.
- **A fingerprint change between pages can invalidate evidence.** The direct test finishes a record after the replacement and asserts `!record_is_current(...)`.
- **Direct inspection records on return; agent tools record on delivery.**
  - In the direct tests, `read_paged` is followed immediately by an assertion on `dependencies()`.
  - The empty-read and failed-read test (`direct_paged_empty_failed_and_redacted_reads_keep_delivery_accounting`) covers empty content, a failed read that records nothing, and a redacted read that records the unredacted source fingerprint.
  - In the agent tests, dependencies travel in the delivery and appear in the context's inspection.
- **Discovery pages record no evidence inputs.**
  - `source_discovery_and_its_pages_do_not_register_reads` pages through `list_sources`, `search_text` and `outline_source` and asserts every delivery and page has empty dependencies. It also asserts the observation callback ran zero times.
  - `source_tools_forward_arguments_and_present_discovery_and_read_results` pages a `search_structure` result. It asserts empty dependencies on every page and that the observation count stays at 3.
- **Preparing an undelivered page records no read.**
  - In the failed-agent scenario of the graph test, `read_node` is requested and the next completion fails. The test asserts `ctx.inspection().dependencies()` is empty. A control case with `contents_of_current_node` and the same failure records one dependency.
  - `direct_page_ids_are_context_scoped_and_unknown_ids_record_nothing` asserts a wrong-context or unknown page records nothing and causes no re-read. `fixed_tools_deliver_domain_contents_with_mandatory_snapshot_dependencies` asserts cross-session and out-of-range pages are errors.

The cited `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs` obligations are exercised in context. Failed reads add no observation, and repeated pages with the same fingerprint do not add duplicates.

I found no plausible violating behavior that these tests would accept.

text: A delivered read page records the dependencies retained by that page under
node or mapped source read retains the original node identity and content
fingerprint; reading a later page does not observe a newer version. A change
to that node's fingerprint can invalidate the evidence even if it happens
between pages. Direct inspection records on return; agent tools record on
delivery. Discovery pages record no evidence inputs, just like their initial
result. Preparing an undelivered page records no read.
Finishing a verification includes every successful tracked node read in its
`Fingerprinted`, whether ordinary code or a model tool requested it. Each observation
contains the node identity and the fingerprint of the contents actually supplied.
A failed read returns an error without inventing a successful observation.
Repeating an identical observation adds no information. Reading the same
identity with two different fingerprints preserves both observations.
